clue.text: Initial move of physician in carriage

indicators.note: the word in tells us the doctor's letters sit inside the word for bearing

parts.note: carriage in the sense of the way one walks or holds oneself is gait
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a qualified doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor makes the opening move of a journey by climbing into a horse-drawn coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' suggests a vehicle, but here it is the way a person walks.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess an opening that sacrifices material for advantage is called this, hence any calculated first step.

clue.text: Creative activity keeping the Parisian on the ball

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the French article goes inside

parts.note: painting, sculpture and the like are art
a Parisian would say le for the

explanation.surface: Someone doing painting while keeping their wits about them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the ball is an idiom for being sharp, watchful and quick to react.

clue.text: Sleeping aid British singer swallowed

indicators.note: swallowed means taken inside, so the abbreviation goes into the singer's word

parts.note: a baritone is a male singer with a middle-range voice

explanation.surface: A British singer has taken a sleeping pill.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites the singer to swallow the pill; in the wordplay the singer swallows the B.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbiturate drug once widely prescribed as a sedative to help people sleep.

clue.text: Vehicle taking circuitous route over top of ridge

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part is placed over, i.e. above, the next
circuitous means roundabout, so the letters of route take an indirect path into a new order
top of picks the opening letter of ridge, the highest letter in a down entry

explanation.surface: A car takes a winding road up and over the crest of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circuitous' tells you to rearrange the letters of route; 'over' works only in a down entry, where that rearrangement sits above the R that 'top of' takes from ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A touring car is an open car built for long-distance pleasure driving.

clue.text: It rescues a lot at sea around first of month

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters wrap about the date
at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of a lot are jumbled

parts.note: the first of February written as a date is 1 Feb, with I as the Roman one

explanation.surface: A rescue craft saves many people out on the ocean at the start of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' turns A LOT into L and OAT, which go 'around' I FEB; 'first of month' is a particular date, 1 February, not the letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat launched to save people in danger at sea is the vessel described.

clue.text: Entertainers do this very fast!

definitions.meaning: performers enjoy the audience who applaud them, read literally as an expression
a British idiom meaning at great speed, as in running flat out

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the phrase: performers are fond of applauders, and the idiom means at top speed, like hammering bell tongues.

clue.text: Anticipated warning over audible display of emotion

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits over, i.e. above, the second

parts.note: golfers shout fore to warn others of a ball in flight

indicators.note: audible means we take the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: making a scene is a public display of emotion

explanation.surface: A warning given above an outburst of feeling that everyone can hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audible' means SCENE is heard and written as SEEN; FORE is the golfer's shout.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee something is to predict it, so an expected event has been predicted.

clue.text: One who shows respect for a lady's private room?

definitions.meaning: someone who bends at the waist in respect
an old word for a woman's private chamber or boudoir

explanation.surface: A courteous man pays respect at the door of a woman's chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who inclines the head shows deference; in poetry and old romance the term also names a lady's inner chamber.

clue.text: Change of attitude regarding make-up

parts.note: regarding means concerning, on the subject of
putting on make-up is putting one's face on

explanation.surface: Someone reconsiders their view of cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete reversal of opinion or policy, from the military command to turn round.

clue.text: Material produced by prophet, a gullible type

parts.note: a seer is someone who foresees the future
a sucker is someone easily fooled

explanation.surface: A soothsayer and a dupe come up with some cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A light puckered cotton fabric with a striped crinkled finish, often used for summer suits.

clue.text: Yarn proceeding from the setter?

definitions.meaning: the weft threads woven across the warp on a loom
the sound a dog such as an Irish setter makes

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the crosswise thread in weaving; the other is a dog's bark, the setter being a breed of hound.

clue.text: Harsh way some books cover revere's enterprise

indicators.note: cover means the two abbreviations sit either side of the journey, enclosing it

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible
Paul Revere's famous midnight ride of 1775 warning of British troops

explanation.surface: A harsh road and some books deal with the American patriot's venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revere' looks like the verb to honour, but it is Paul Revere, whose ride is a famous episode of American history.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud grating sound or forceful tone is shrill and jarring.

clue.text: Guarantee time in county with only one river

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for time inside the shortened county
with only one means a doubled letter is reduced to a single copy

parts.note: Surrey is a county south of London

explanation.surface: A pledge made at some point in a county that has just one river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with only one' strips one of the two Rs from SURREY, leaving SUREY, and T goes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or sum standing as security for another's obligation, so a guarantor or pledge.

clue.text: Drive away, not completing photographic assignment

indicators.note: not completing means the word stops short of its final letter

parts.note: a photo session is called a shoot

explanation.surface: A photographer heads off before finishing the session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not completing' drops the T from SHOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as an exclamation to scare off animals or people, and as a verb meaning to send them packing.

clue.text: Hack is shown over Oxford, possibly? Lucky thing

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part is placed over, above, the second

parts.note: a hack is a horse for ordinary riding
an Oxford is a style of laced leather shoe

explanation.surface: A journalist is shown around Oxford and finds a lucky charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' suggests a reporter and 'Oxford' the city; they are a riding horse and a type of shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped iron nailed to a hoof, traditionally hung over doors as a charm for good luck.

clue.text: Lines written by graduate in impartial morality play

indicators.note: in places the lines and the graduate inside the word for fair

parts.note: even means fair, not favouring either side
RY, railway, gives lines of track
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate's degree

explanation.surface: A graduate writes lines for a fair-minded medieval drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' are railway lines, RY; 'written by' simply joins RY to MA.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a fifteenth-century English allegorical drama about a soul facing death and judgement.

clue.text: A time when those worldly-wise were not born?

definitions.text: A time when those worldly-wise were not born?

parts.words: A time when those worldly-wise were not born?
parts.note: the idiom says a shrewd person was not born the day before today, read literally as a date

explanation.definitionFit: The day before today, the time of the idiom about knowing people not being naive.

clue.text: Raising objections natural, being obstinate

indicators.note: Raising, in a down clue, means the word is turned upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: ifs and buts: buts are objections
a natural talent is born to it

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps making objections is naturally pig-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwilling to change position, dogged and refusing to give way.

clue.text: Non-European unexpectedly into Lear

indicators.note: unexpectedly signals the letters of into Lear turning up in a surprising order

explanation.surface: A foreigner bursts in on King Lear without warning.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for Eastern, especially from East Asia, as opposed to Western.

clue.text: Staunch branch of family

definitions.meaning: to stop a flow, as of blood
a line of descent from a common ancestor

explanation.surface: A loyal offshoot of the family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to check or halt a flow; the other is a lineage, a main line of a family tree.

clue.text: Question soldiers with hesitation, the smallest number acceptable

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Questioning troops who hesitate yields the minimum needed for a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The minimum count of members who must be present for a meeting to conduct business validly.

clue.text: Producer's last note about device in recording studio

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word Producer
about means turned round, so the musical note is read backwards

parts.note: a breve is a long musical note

explanation.surface: A record producer's final note concerns some studio equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it is the reversal signal; a breve is a long note in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for reverberation, an echo effect added to sound by electronic studio equipment.

clue.text: Hole in heart treated

indicators.note: treated suggests the letters of heart are worked on, rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A surgeon repairs a hole in someone's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hole in heart' looks like a medical condition; 'Hole' is the definition and 'in' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox's or badger's burrow is called this, a hole in the ground where it lives.

clue.text: Silk fabric jazz singer displayed after quiet season

indicators.note: displayed after means the singer comes behind the other pieces

parts.note: p, piano, means quiet in music
a season of shows is a run
Ella Fitzgerald, the American jazz singer

explanation.surface: A jazz singer shows off silk material after a quiet season.
explanation.walkthrough: A RUN is a season of performances; ELLA is Ella Fitzgerald.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong silk or worsted twill once used for clergy gowns and shoe uppers.

clue.text: Thrust from back of van into toboggan

indicators.note: into means the letter goes inside the sledge's name

parts.note: a luge is a small racing sledge

indicators.note: back of picks the final letter of van

explanation.surface: A thrust from the rear of a van sends it onto a sledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of' gives N from van, which goes 'into' LUGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden forward movement, as in fencing or attacking, is a thrust.

clue.text: Burn fish daily

definitions.meaning: to scorch or blacken by fire
a trout-like fish of cold lakes
a daily is a British cleaning woman who comes in each day

explanation.surface: Burn the fish every day.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: to scorch, a freshwater relative of the trout, and a cleaner, 'daily' being British for a domestic help.

clue.text: Deliveries part of Yorkshire once found most important

parts.note: in cricket a set of six balls bowled by one bowler has its own name
Yorkshire was formerly divided into three Ridings, North, East and West

explanation.surface: Balls bowled in a once-divided English county found to be crucial.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler's six deliveries make an OVER; Yorkshire, a northern English county, had three Ridings until 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking precedence over all else, so dominant or paramount.

clue.text: The misguided in fur coats, I feel …

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the furs

parts.note: minks are fur coats

indicators.note: misguided means led astray, so the letters of the are shuffled

explanation.surface: The wrongheaded people in fur coats, I think…
explanation.walkthrough: 'misguided' makes ETH from THE, which goes 'in' MINKS.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic way of saying it seems to me, so a formal way of offering an opinion.

clue.text: … Will possibly hesitate, creating havoc

parts.note: may and will are both modal verbs expressing possibility, so one stands for the other
to hem and haw is to hesitate

explanation.surface: Will possibly hesitates and causes chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a man's name, but it is the verb, standing for another verb of possibility.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent disorder and confusion, a scene of chaos.
